text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most buyers.** The sources I found broadly agree on this.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 2,000-6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-1,000 for NMC. Used daily, that is about 8 years versus under 2. ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/))
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells ran cooler and failed less violently, with smoke rather than flames. That matters for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle. LFP isn't fireproof, though, and one study found it reached runaway sooner in overcharge. ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc))
- **Cost:** LFP is cheaper to make, and one retailer's data shows a median of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC. Cost per rated cycle favors LFP even more. ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc))

**Where NMC wins**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per pound. But in finished stations the gap is much smaller, roughly 10-16% in two databases, because the case, inverter and fans weigh the same either way. Some LFP stations are lighter per Wh than some NMC ones. ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/))

**Caveats**
- **Cycle ratings aren't standardized.** Check whether a rating is to 70% or 80% capacity, since 70% is a weaker promise.
- **Cold weather depends on the maker, not the chemistry.** Both LFP and NMC stations typically refuse to charge below 32°F. Some sources claim NMC is much worse in the cold, but the manuals-based sources say the difference is small. Check your model's manual.
- **Don't replace a working NMC unit.** For rare use, such as a few outages a year, an NMC unit will likely age out from time before it runs out of cycles.

**Bottom line:** Buy LFP for daily or frequent use, home backup, or keeping it indoors. NMC only makes sense for a deeply discounted, lightly used unit, or when every pound matters. Almost all current stations are LFP anyway, so just confirm the chemistry on the spec sheet.
